evals.prompt: I'm migrating our iOS app from Mapbox Maps SDK v10 to v11. Our store map uses a UITapGestureRecognizer on the MapView, then calls mapView.mapboxMap.queryRenderedFeatures(with: point, options: RenderedQueryOptions(layerIds: ["stores"], filter: nil)) and opens the first feature. The v11 migration guide shows gestures.onLayerTap for this. Should I just switch to onLayerTap?
expectations: Says onLayerTap (and onMapTap) are deprecated in current v11 releases (from 11.13), so porting to them leaves the app on a deprecated API
Recommends Featureset Interactions: mapboxMap.addInteraction(TapInteraction(.layer("stores")) { feature, context in ... return true })
Explains that returning true stops the tap propagating to features below
Uses [weak self] in the interaction closure, or warns about retain cycles
Mentions onLayerTap only as a fallback if the app pins an 11.x older than 11.13

evals.prompt: Our iOS app creates the map with `let mapView = MapView(frame: view.bounds)` and never sets a style. We just bumped MapboxMaps to 11.x and fixed the compile errors. Anything else we should check before shipping?
expectations: Points out that v11 changed the default style from Mapbox Streets to Mapbox Standard, so the map will look different
Presents it as a decision for the developer, not a silent change, and recommends keeping v10's look by default

Shows setting the style explicitly at creation via MapInitOptions(styleURI:), pinned to the literal Streets URI the v10 SDK used (not just the .streets constant, which may resolve to a newer version in v11)
Does not recommend moving to Standard as part of the migration (only as a separate opt-in)
Mentions other runtime behavior changes such as puckBearingEnabled now defaulting to false

evals.prompt: How much work would it be to move our Android app from Mapbox Maps SDK v10 to v11? I don't want any code changed yet, just an estimate. The app uses a MapView in XML layouts, point annotations, a click listener that queries rendered features, a GeoJSON source we rebuild when the user selects a store, and the location component.
expectations: Follows the inventory and plan steps only and explicitly doesn't change code
Groups the work by area (setup and token, map view and style, annotations, style and sources, gestures and interactions, location) with an effort estimate per area
Identifies the click listener plus queryRenderedFeatures tap handling as moving to Featureset Interactions (ClickInteraction), not a literal port
Identifies the selection-by-rebuilding-the-source pattern and recommends feature state (and/or partial GeoJSON updates) as the v11 target
Lists behavior changes as decisions, including the default style becoming Standard, and states blockers or that there are none

evals.prompt: Migrating iOS Maps SDK v10 to v11. I replaced `mapView.mapboxMap.onNext(event: .styleLoaded) { _ in self.addLayers() }` with `_ = mapView.mapboxMap.onStyleLoaded.observeNext { _ in self.addLayers() }` and now my layers never show up. No errors. What's wrong?
expectations: Explains that observe/observeNext return an AnyCancelable that cancels the subscription when it is released, so discarding it with `_ =` cancels the observer at once
Shows storing the token, e.g. `.store(in: &cancelables)` with a `Set<AnyCancelable>` property
Recommends [weak self] in the handler
Does not claim the plain Cancelable from ease/fly/addInteraction behaves the same way, or doesn't mention it

evals.prompt: We're moving our iOS navigation-style app to Maps SDK v11. In v10 we set mapView.location.options.distanceFilter = 50 and the puck rotated with the device heading. After the upgrade the puck no longer rotates and the distanceFilter line doesn't compile. Fix it without changing what users see.
expectations: Explains LocationManager options now only control the puck; provider settings like distanceFilter move to an AppleLocationProvider installed with mapView.location.override(provider:)
Explains puckBearingEnabled now defaults to false in v11 and sets mapView.location.options.puckBearingEnabled = true to keep v10 behavior
Records or presents the bearing change as a behavior decision rather than silently changing it
Mentions that heading now comes from a separate HeadingProvider if the app uses a custom location provider

evals.prompt: While migrating our Android app to Maps SDK v11 can you also switch us to Mapbox Standard and turn on 3D buildings? It seems like the right time.
expectations: Keeps the style change out of the SDK migration and explains why (separate, opt-in change; may change look and data products)
Offers to do the Standard move as a separate step or project after the migration is verified
Still pins the app's current style explicitly during the migration because v11 defaults to Standard
